issues.issue: Did the RPD properly find no objective basis for the forced-priesthood fear?
issues.applicant_position: No rational basis to prefer the Leiden and London professors over the SIU professor; an objective basis exists.
issues.result_text: Documents show no serious persecution risk from family; SIU opinion too vague; divine consequences alone insufficient.

issues.issue: Did the altered affidavit and the BOC omission about loss of kingship undermine her credibility?
issues.applicant_position: Not asked about the second affidavit's swearing; no material difference; RPD speculated about alteration.
issues.result_text: Affidavit was altered after sealing, neither version is credible, and the kingship omission was not explained.

issues.issue: Did her limited knowledge of the cult undermine her credibility?
issues.applicant_position: Secrecy and her Christian upbringing made it unreasonable to expect detailed cult knowledge.
issues.result_text: Six years living with her cult-priest father made basic knowledge expected; her knowledge was inadequate.

issues.issue: Did the RPD fail to assess the section 97 risk of life or cruel treatment?
issues.applicant_position: RPD failed to assess s.97 risk from a forced chief-priest role and did not consider the totality of evidence.
issues.result_text: RPD did turn its mind to s.97; without credibility the s.97 claim cannot stand, so no error.
